FOURTH OCCURRENCE — same worker-crash signature, a SECOND unrelated change.

2026-08-07 22:06 UTC, change 1512 (ticket 9f63), patch set 7, run 31221438184 — the ONLY failing job:
  pytest (ubuntu-latest, py3.11): FAILED tests/unit/test_opcert_service_app.py::test_matching_guard_is_accepted - worker 'gw3' crashed

Identical test, worker id and cell to the two occurrences on change 1520 (ticket e6e9). Two unrelated changes, two agents, four runs. Neither change touches the opcert service — 1512 changes reconciler cursor handling, 1520 changed the Jira arbitration baseline. The common factor is the matrix cell.

STRONG ROOT-CAUSE LEAD: this file was SKIPPED in CI entirely until 604e4e5d67 (ticket 599e) landed TODAY — no lane installed the reviewbot/ui extras, so every test in it was silently skipped. Its exposure to the parallel runner is therefore BRAND NEW. A test that never ran under '-n 4 --dist worksteal' before is now running in it and killing a worker. That timing is unlikely to be coincidence, and it reframes the bug: not 'this test regressed' but 'this test was never exercised in the parallel runner and does not survive it'. Suspect process/socket state in a FastAPI service test under xdist — the failure is a WORKER DEATH, not an assertion.

Cost: each occurrence burns a full CI cycle (~70 min) on an otherwise-green change; 1512 PS7 already holds LLM-Review +1 (PASS). The remedy both times was a content-free rebase/recheck — pure retry — so it is an infrastructure tax charged to unrelated authors, the same shape as the cancelled-run problem where an innocent change reads as rejected.

Options, cheapest first: (1) quarantine this file from the parallel selection on py3.11 only — it passes standalone in 0.88s, so serialising it is nearly free; (2) root-cause the xdist worker death, starting from the 599e exposure lead above; (3) move py3.11 to an advisory lane, keeping 3.12/3.13 gating.

This ticket is closed (its 99%-hang was genuinely fixed); recorded here to keep the cell's history together, but a live recurring CI blocker likely needs its own open ticket.
